description: How investment, architecture, delivery, operations, data, transactions and software partners coordinate across Enable U-style managed integration outcomes.

relationTypes.name: Mandate
relationTypes.description: Sets investment, architecture or service constraints.

relationTypes.name: Delivery
relationTypes.description: Designs, builds, certifies or hands over an integration outcome.

relationTypes.name: Service
relationTypes.description: Operates, escalates and improves live chains.

relationTypes.name: Information
relationTypes.description: Shares contracts, lineage, status and evidence.

relations.name: Funds and constrains the target landscape
relations.description: The CIO sets service priorities, risk appetite, data-residency constraints and migration funding; the architect translates them into executable patterns and waves.

relations.name: Provides contracts, patterns and exceptions
relations.description: The architect publishes approved patterns and contracts; the developer returns implementation evidence and requests explicit exceptions where reality differs.

relations.name: Hands over an observable service
relations.description: Delivery supplies deployed version, dashboard, owner, runbook, rollback and known failure behavior; operations accepts only when the business signal is visible.

relations.name: Feeds runtime residue into architecture
relations.description: Incidents, dependency degradation, policy drift and recurring manual work become evidence for pattern and portfolio changes.

relations.name: Defines ownership and data contracts
relations.description: The data owner supplies purpose, classification, quality and lineage requirements; the architect ensures integration contracts preserve them.

relations.name: Escalates business transaction exceptions
relations.description: Finance and payroll operations own the legal business decision while service operations owns delivery, network and replay diagnostics.

relations.name: Co-builds and certifies reusable connectors
relations.description: The ISV owns product semantics and versions; the integration developer owns managed-boundary behavior, tests and operability.

relations.name: Shares lifecycle and escalation responsibility
relations.description: Both parties maintain a version and escalation map so customers encounter one support path instead of supplier deadlock.
